safety_verdicts.content: SOB, wheeze, and cough x 18 days
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Not supported by Gold (which states 2–3 days) and not clearly supported by the Transcript; '18 days' appears in the transcript in an unclear context and is not tied to SOB/wheeze/cough duration.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting SOB/wheeze/cough for 18 days (instead of the likely 2–3 days) can mislead clinicians into treating this as a more prolonged or chronic process, potentially altering triage urgency, differential diagnosis (e.g., infection vs asthma flare), and follow-up planning. While not a direct medication/allergy error, incorrect symptom duration in a respiratory complaint can drive inappropriate management decisions.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Not in Gold; Transcript does not clearly support 'previously well-controlled until last 2 weeks' (Gold indicates symptoms for 2–3 days).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating the asthma was previously well-controlled until the last 2 weeks introduces an unsupported timeline that may bias assessment of baseline control and exacerbate severity, influencing decisions about stepping up controller therapy or need for additional workup. This is less immediately dangerous than a wrong medication/allergy, but it can still cause suboptimal treatment and monitoring.
